# Bazel vs zel code differences: core build engine

Category rule: Skyframe, analysis, packages, actions, VFS, utilities, concurrency, graphs, and other core Java implementation not assigned to a narrower subsystem.

- Failure entries: 1620
- Missing: 880
- Partial: 740
- Source review: Bazel 9.3.2 (`5951e93c05876016377063a150f8b56f38276461`) versus zel (`2084b3f5a9bd343f38ffbc7633d65f21bab0f654`)
- Complete review: [bazel-code-differences.md](bazel-code-differences.md)

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/ApiExporter.java`
- Bazel lines: 435
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no `docgen` package and no Starlark builtins exporter.
  - [P3] `main` requires `-m` link map, `-p` rule-class provider, `-f` output, and at least one `-i` Java dir or `--be_stardoc_proto`. It loads `SymbolFamilies` and writes a binary `Builtins` proto.
  - [P3] Type pages export members sorted by case-sensitive name. Constructors are skipped as type fields. `native` methods are emitted as both `BUILD` globals and `BZL` fields. Native rules are extra `BZL` fields on `native` and also `BUILD` globals, each callable with a mandatory `name` plus rule attributes.
  - [P3] Globals unwrap `GuardedValue`. Callables use `MemberDoc` when present, otherwise a `StarlarkFunction` signature, a `BuiltinFunction` annotation, or a synthetic `**kwargs` callable. `None` is typed `NoneType`. `True` and `False` are typed `bool`. `_builtins_dummy` is ignored.
  - [P3] Signatures mark `*args` and `**kwargs`, copy defaults, and treat parameters without a default as mandatory. Undocumented annotated parameters are dropped. An implicit `*` is inserted when a parameter is named-only.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/BuildDocCollector.java`
- Bazel lines: 493
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] `BuildDocCollector` reads a `#`-comment deny list, walks Java sources for doc comments, then overlays `stardoc_output.ModuleInfo` protos, which take precedence. It warns on rule overrides and indexes rule families for `RuleLinkExpander`.
  - [P3] For Java-sourced native rules it picks the closest documented ancestor attribute and otherwise fills binary, test, common, or typical predefined attributes. For Starlark rules it injects those same sets, skips the implicit `name` attribute, maps empty docstrings onto typical attributes, and flags deprecated docstrings.
  - [P3] Zel has no docgen collector. `starlark_doc_extract` only declares proto outputs and analyzes as `extra_action_like`, which emits no files. `stardoc_output.proto` is embedded but never parsed into rule docs. `#:` doc comments are explicitly not ported. Encyclopedia flags (`--denylist`, `--input_dir`, `--be_stardoc_proto`) are absent.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/BuildEncyclopediaOptions.java`
- Bazel lines: 106
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no Build Encyclopedia docgen tool and does not define or parse this options class.
  - [P3] `--input_dir`/`-i` is a repeatable list of Java source directories. `--input_root`/`-r` is the source-tree root, required because the link-map schema depends on the execution platform. `--be_stardoc_proto` (old name `--input_stardoc_proto`) is a repeatable list of `ModuleInfo` binary protos; those docs override `--input_dir`.
  - [P3] `--provider`/`-p` is the rule-class provider name. `--output_file`/`-f` and `--output_dir`/`-o` (default `.`) choose the generated output. `--denylist` (old name `--blacklist`, `-b`) is a file of rules to omit. `--single_page`/`-1` writes one HTML page and is mutually exclusive with `--create_toc`.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/BuildEncyclopediaProcessor.java`
- Bazel lines: 251
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no assembler that groups rule docs into language-specific versus generic families or writes encyclopedia pages. Vendored Stardoc only renders Starlark protos.
  - [P3] `generateDocumentation` scans Java dirs plus Stardoc `ModuleInfo` protos (protos override Java), applies a deny list, and writes under `outputDir`.
  - [P3] Families are split by `RuleDocumentation.isLanguageSpecific()`. Mixing language-specific and generic rules in one family throws `BuildEncyclopediaDocException`. The overview uses the two lists separately. Other pages use language-specific families followed by generic ones.
  - [P3] A rule present in `ConfiguredRuleClassProvider` is included only when `RuleClass.isDocumented()`. A name missing from that map is still included. Names containing `$` are dropped from the undocumented-rule warning. Remaining names are sorted and printed to stderr.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/DocCheckerUtils.java`
- Bazel lines: 96
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no HTML-tag checker for documentation. `UNCHECKED_HTML_TAGS` is `"br"`, `"li"`, `"ul"`, and `"p"`.
  - [P3] `TAG_PATTERN` is `"<([/]?[a-z0-9_]+)([^>]*)>"` with `CASE_INSENSITIVE`. `COMMENT_OR_BACKTICK_PATTERN` is `"<!--.*?-->|`.*`"`. Matches are stripped with `replaceAll("")` before tag matching, so comments and backticks are not checked. `.` does not match newlines unless `DOTALL` is set, so a multi-line HTML comment is not stripped.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/PredefinedAttributes.java`
- Bazel lines: 116
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-packages/src/rule_class.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P3] Bazel loads 29 classpath HTML templates (`templates/attributes/{test,typical,common,binary}/*.html`) into `RuleDocumentationAttribute` maps. Zel has no attribute HTML templates and no encyclopedia generator.
  - [P3] Documented common names are `aspect_hints`, `compatible_with`, `deprecation`, `exec_compatible_with`, `exec_group_compatible_with`, `exec_properties`, `features`, `package_metadata`, `restricted_to`, `tags`, `target_compatible_with`, `testonly`, `toolchains`, and `visibility`. The `@starlark` schema has all 14, plus `expect_failure`, `transitive_configs`, `generator_name`, `generator_function`, `generator_location`, `:action_listener`, and `$config_dependencies`. Hand-written `common_attrs` omits `exec_group_compatible_with` and adds `name`, `applicable_licenses`, `licenses`, and `distribs`.
  - [P1] Documented test names are `args`, `env`, `env_inherit`, `size`, `timeout`, `flaky`, `shard_count`, and `local`. Live `@starlark:test` has `size`, `timeout`, `flaky`, `shard_count`, `local`, and `args`, and does not define `env` or `env_inherit`. Hand-written `test_attrs` includes `env` and `env_inherit`, but `Builder::test` has no callers.
  - [P1] Documented binary names are `args`, `env`, and `output_licenses`. Live `@starlark:executable` has `args` and `output_licenses` only. Hand-written `binary_attrs` includes `env`, but `Builder::binary` has no callers.
  - [P3] Typical docs (`data`, `deps`, `licenses`, `srcs`) have no shared Zel list. `licenses` is on `common_attrs` instead of a typical-only catalog. Empty-docstring linking to the typical table has no counterpart.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/RuleDocumentation.java`
- Bazel lines: 385
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no encyclopedia rule model holding name, `RuleType`, family, raw HTML, source URL, flags, `${var}` doc variables, and a `TreeSet` of attributes.
  - [P3] This class never HTML-escapes. `getAttributeSignature` interpolates names into element text and `href` fragments with `String.format` only. Fragments are lowercased, not percent-encoded.
  - [P3] `normalize` is a filename rewrite: ASCII lower case, `+` to `p`, drop `()`, whitespace and `/` to `-`, collapse repeated `-` (`"C / C++"` to `"c-cpp"`).
  - [P3] `getHtmlDocumentation` replaces `${key}` with the raw variable value. `VAR_IMPLICIT_OUTPUTS` is wrapped in an `<h4>` and inserted as HTML. A set `RuleLinkExpander` then expands the result. `IllegalArgumentException` becomes `BuildEncyclopediaDocException`.
  - [P3] `getCommandLineDocumentation` does not call `getHtmlDocumentation`. `toCommandLineFormat` strips tags (`<br>` to newline, `<a href>` to the URL, other tags removed, `${word}` deleted) and leaves HTML entities as written.
  - [P3] `FLAG_GENERIC_RULE` forces `RuleType.OTHER`. Any other unknown type throws `Invalid rule type`. Equality is `ruleName` only. Order is type priority (FLAG, BINARY, LIBRARY, TEST, OTHER) then name. Doc-variable substitution follows `HashMap` iteration order.
  - [P3] Zel’s `html_escape` encodes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'` for option help, not rule pages. Implicit outputs are `%{name}` / `%{attr}` templates, not `${var}` HTML substitution.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/RuleLinkExpander.java`
- Bazel lines: 252
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no `${link …}` expander. The only `${link …}` text under the Zel tree is unexpanded HTML in third-party `.bzl` docs. Stardoc’s `MarkdownRenderer` does not implement this class.
  - [P3] The dot pass matches `\$\{link (([a-zA-Z_-]+)(\.([a-zA-Z_\.-]+))?)\}`. The heading pass matches `\$\{link (([a-zA-Z_-]+)\#([a-zA-Z0-9_\.-]+))\}`. `expand` runs the dot pass, then the `#` pass.
  - [P3] Multi-page rule links become `Paths.get(beRoot, "<family>.html#<ref>")` (OS separators, BE root prepended). Multi-page heading links are `family + ".html#" + heading` with no `beRoot`. Single-page rule links are `#` plus the full ref. Single-page heading links are `#` plus the heading only.

  - [P3] A dotted attribute on a static page throws and demands `${link static-page#heading}`. `common-definitions` and `make-variables` on a single page become `#name` or `#heading` and ignore the mapping. Unknown names throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Replacements go through `Matcher.quoteReplacement`.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/SourceFileReader.java`
- Bazel lines: 372
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] Zel has no `#BLAZE_RULE`, `#BLAZE_RULE_VAR`, `#BLAZE_RULE_ATTR`, or family-summary scan. Help text comes from option definitions, not Java source comments.
  - [P3] Charset is hard-coded UTF-8. A bad sequence fails the read under the UTF-8 decoder’s default REPORT action. Zel treats the Bazel server default as ISO-8859-1 and counts Starlark source columns as Latin-1.
  - [P3] If the path is neither a file nor a classpath resource, `readTextFile` prints `Couldn't find file or resource: ...` to stdout and returns. Docs stay empty. It does not throw.
  - [P3] In-block lines are kept after `replaceAll("^[\\s]*\\*", "")`. That strips leading whitespace and one `*` only. `//` is left in place. The start-marker line is not part of the body.
  - [P3] `endFamilySummary` saves the buffer but never clears `inFamilySummary` or the buffer, so after the first end marker later lines keep appending and a later end marker replaces `familySummary` with the growing buffer.
  - [P3] `checkDocValidity` rejects a new rule, variable, or attribute while one of those is already open, and the message always says `#BLAZE_RULE`. An open family summary is not treated as overlap. A variable must name a rule documented in the same file.
  - [P3] `readTemplateContents` replaces `${KEY}` with sequential `String.replace` (no recursion, no escape). A null map, or a line with no `${`, is copied unchanged. Every line, including the last, is followed by the line separator.
  - [P3] Rule flags are `split(",")` with no trim, or an empty set if the flag matcher misses. A bad header pair is a `System.err.printf` WARNING with no newline.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/SourceUrlMapper.java`
- Bazel lines: 103
- Zel counterpart: `none`

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/docgen/StarlarkDocumentationCollector.java`
- Bazel lines: 518
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - [P3] `getAllDocPages` caches one category map. It parses each `--api_stardoc_proto` `ModuleInfo` and scans `com/google/devtools/build` plus `net/starlark/java` via `Classpath.findClasses`. Zel has no classpath scan or page cache.
  - [P3] Collection order is builtins (`documented=true`, subclass wins when docs match, unrelated same-name builtins throw), then ordinary methods (skip `@StarlarkConstructor`; struct fields that return a self-call constructor are rewritten), then `@GlobalMethods` plus a hard-coded `MethodLibrary` treated as `Environment.ALL`, then constructors. Zel’s builtins are runtime values only.
  - [P3] `.bzl` API protos become `TOP_LEVEL_MODULE` struct pages (top-level `struct` symbols only; a `.bzl` struct may override a Java module, with a warning, and a second `.bzl` definition is an error) and `PROVIDER` pages. Functions must be `struct.name`. `#:` doc comments are required on the struct. Nested structs are skipped. Aspects, macros, module extensions, repository rules, and rules are rejected. The module-extension error text says `module extesions`.
  - [P3] A `TypeParser` is built from page names, skipping `CONFIGURATION_FRAGMENT` because those names clash with built-in modules. Pages in each category are sorted by title with `Collator` for `Locale.US`.
  - [P3] The native `starlark_doc_extract` rule lists the proto outputs, but `extra_action_like` emits no proto and no files, so the input this collector reads is not produced.

A non-empty conflict map sets a global flag and replaces that visited set with an empty one. A later key whose own map is empty then reruns its full transitive closure with a private visited set and does not take a place in the latch chain. The key that discovered the conflict, and the first key (`toWaitFor == null`), do not rerun.
  - [P1] Null Sky values are skipped. Non-`ActionLookupKey` deps are not traversed. `InterruptedException` from the graph sets the interrupt flag and returns. A rejected action-registration task (pool already shut down) is ignored. `shutdown()` waits for the exclusive pool, then interruptibly shuts down the free pool, and restores the interrupt status.
  - [P1] Each action is registered concurrently. An exact `ActionConflictException` stores only that action and skips its prefix checks; the same action can overwrite a previous entry. An interrupt during registration sets the interrupt flag and drops the rest of that lookup value’s actions. A prefix `ActionConflictException` from the trie walk is wrapped as `IllegalStateException`. A failure of the collected futures becomes `IllegalStateException("Unexpected exception")`.
  - [P1] Prefix checks use a `ConcurrentHashMap` segment trie and keep only the shorter path. The artifact named for a conflicting subtree is whichever child `ConcurrentHashMap` iteration returns first. A conflict is recorded for both the prior and current actions under one prefix exception, then that path stops. A runfiles tree and its `MANIFEST` child are not a conflict. `conflictCheckPerAction` throws that exception when no bad-action map is passed, and a missing generating action fails with a null check.
  - [P1] Zel’s prefix scan is a sorted full comparison of exec-path strings, returns a single error, does not exempt runfiles pairs, does not retain the shorter path for later checks, and does not continue to other actions.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/OptionsParsingResult.java`
- Bazel lines: 121
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/parser.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P1] `getOptionValueDescription` and `containsExplicitOption` resolve the canonical name and the old name, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with `No such option '<name>'` when the name is unknown, and return null / false when the option exists but was never set. Zel `parsed_options` is keyed only by the canonical name, and `get_bool` / `get_str` / `get_int` return `None` for both unknown and unset names.
  - [P1] `asListOfOptionValues` lists every registered option, inserting a default `OptionValueDescription` for unset ones, in options-class registration order. `allOptionValues` lists only options that were assigned, in that same registration order. Zel keeps only assigned options in a `BTreeMap` iterated by name.
  - [P1] `asCompleteListOfParsedOptions` returns every parsed instance, including repeats, expansions, hidden, undocumented, and implicit options, stable-sorted by `OptionPriority`. `asListOfExplicitOptions` keeps the explicit subset. `asListOfCanonicalOptions` keeps only instances that still contribute to the final value, drops values overridden at equal or higher priority, drops expansion parents, and drops instances that have an implicit dependent, then sorts by priority. Zel stores one `OptionValueDescription` per name and appends `canonical_flags` in encounter order, with no explicit-versus-canonical split.
  - [P1] `canonicalize` emits `getDeprecatedCanonicalForm` of those canonical instances in priority order: booleans are `--name=1` or `--name=0`, other options are `--name=<unconverted value>`, and a void option’s null unconverted value is formatted as `--name=null`. Expansion parents are omitted and implicit requirements are omitted. Zel records the expansion flag itself when it is not void, records implicit-requirement children, omits void options, and `canonicalize_flags` dedups single-value flags to the last `canonical_flags` entry. Invocation-policy `SetValue` overwrites `parsed_options` without updating `canonical_flags`, so the canonical list can still show the overridden user flag.
  - [P1] `getResidue` is every non-option token before and after `--`. `getPreDoubleDashResidue` returns that full list when nothing followed `--`; otherwise it drops every residue element whose string `List.contains` matches any post-`--` token, including a distinct pre-`--` copy of the same string. Zel puts non-options in `targets`. After `--`, `run` moves the first token into `targets` only when `targets` is empty and the rest into `passthrough_args`; every other command appends all post-`--` tokens to `targets`.
  - [P1] `getSkippedArgs` returns the arguments skipped because they matched a skipped prefix, or an empty list. Zel has no skipped-prefix result.
  - [P1] `getAliases` is a copy of a `HashMap` filled from parsed `--flag_alias` values, so iteration order is hash order. Zel `flag_aliases` is a `BTreeMap` iterated by alias name.
  - [P1] `success` stays on the result object and defaults to true until `setError` clears it, so a caller can hold a parsed result with `success() == false`. Zel `parse` returns `Result` and does not expose a success flag on a populated `ParsedCommandOptions`.
  - [P1] Inherited `getStarlarkOptions` is an `ImmutableSortedMap` left empty by the native parser and filled separately. Starlark values are not part of `OptionsParsingResult.canonicalize`. Zel stores every `--//` / `--@` flag in a name-sorted `BTreeMap` (last assignment wins) plus an occurrence vector, and also appends `--name=value` (bare flags forced to `=true` or `=false`) onto `canonical_flags`.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/OptionsUsage.java`
- Bazel lines: 237
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-server/src/commands/help.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] `paragraphFill` wraps with `BreakIterator.getLineInstance()` (default locale). Segment length is a UTF-16 `String.length()`, and `word.length() + cursor > width` is a signed 32-bit sum. Spaces the iterator keeps on a segment stay in the output, so a wrapped line can end with a space and an empty paragraph is an indent-only line of spaces. `paragraph_fill` breaks only after runs of U+0020, after `-` between alphanumeric scalars, and after `/` when the next scalar is a letter. It counts Unicode scalars (`chars().count()`) in a `usize` sum, and it pops trailing spaces and tabs before a wrap and at the end of every paragraph, so those trailing break spaces and the indent on a blank or over-long first segment are removed.
  - [P2] `getUsage(Class, StringBuilder)` appends every option of that class, including undocumented ones, sorted only by option name, at `HelpVerbosity.LONG`, with tags omitted and with no category headings. Nothing in zel does that. `describe_options` groups documented options by documentation category and calls `option_usage` with `include_tags` true.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/ParsedOptionDescription.java`
- Bazel lines: 226
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/parser.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - [P2] Bazel stores each occurrence with a command-line form, an unconverted value, an origin (priority, source, implicit dependent, expanded-from), a conversion context, and `oldNameUsed`. Non-dummy factories require a non-null command-line form, and a null definition or origin is rejected. Zel keeps one `OptionValueDescription` per option name plus `canonical_flags` strings, so there is no dummy instance, origin chain, conversion context, or old-name bit, and `isExplicit` (both expanded-from and implicit-dependent null, and source not ending in `PROJECT.scl`) is never applied.
  - [P1] `getCanonicalForm` for `boolean.class` is `--<name>` or `--no<name>` from the converted boolean. A conversion failure is thrown as `RuntimeException` with message `Unexpected parsing exception`. Zel records only the deprecated `--<name>=1` or `--<name>=0` form.
  - [P1] `getCanonicalFormWithValueEscaper` leaves a null unconverted value as `--<name>` (void options) and otherwise appends `=` plus the escaper result (`ShellEscaper` at the call site). `getDeprecatedCanonicalForm` always formats `--%s=%s`, so a null value becomes the text `null`. Zel leaves values unescaped and omits `Void` options from `canonical_flags`.
  - [P1] A boolean-syntax flag with no explicit value is stored for `getUnconvertedValue` as `1` or `0`. Zel stores `true` or `false` and rewrites only the canonical string to `1` or `0`. An explicit `--flag=<text>` stays that text in both.
  - [P1] `getConvertedValue` rethrows `OptionsParsingException` with message `While parsing option <commandLineForm>: <cause message>` (a null form renders as the word `null`) and the converter exception as the cause. Zel uses that prefix while parsing and replaces the error, dropping the cause.
  - [P2] `toString` is the definition text `option '--<name>'` when the command-line form is null, and otherwise `option '<form>'` plus ` (source <source>)` when the origin source is non-null. Zel does not emit that description.
  - [P1] `isHidden` is true when the metadata tags contain `HIDDEN` or `INTERNAL`. `isDocumented` requires a category other than `UNDOCUMENTED` and a false `isHidden`. Zel does not apply those predicates to a parsed option.
